doctrine: Golden vectors pinning what `mod` means on BOTH sides of the FFI seam.
`least_non_negative_residue` is the value this estate means by `mod`. It
is what a cyclic group of order n means, and what Python's `%` computes.
`truncated_remainder` is what Rust, C, C++, Java and Go compute with `%`:
the sign follows the dividend, not the divisor. It is recorded here NOT
as an alternative but as the wrong answer a re-implementation produces by
default -- so a test can assert against it, not merely for the right one.
A test that only checks the correct value passes on a host that has
never been asked the question.
The hazard this closes: a Rust re-derivation of a row Python already
re-derived would disagree, and the disagreement surfaces as a
CONTRADICTED row -- the PRODUCER blamed for a difference between two
hosts.
Both sides read this file. Neither side transcribes the numbers. The
values were computed, not written by hand: a hand-written fixture in
this module already claimed 10^30 mod 7 = 6 (it is 1) and was caught by
the implementation it was meant to check.
Cases where the two conventions AGREE are kept deliberately. A vector
set containing only disagreements would pass a host that returned the
least non-negative residue for negatives and garbage for positives.
